time_scope: Eades 1979 lexical data reanalyzed by Sherer
claim: Root-internal consonant sequences are predominantly either homorganic sequences or sequences beginning with an apical consonant followed by a non-apical consonant.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Rare laminal-nasal-initial sequences and the sequences wg and m+velar-nasal do not fit the main generalizations and are tracked separately.

time_scope: Eades 1979 lexical data reanalyzed by Sherer
claim: Three laminal-nasal-initial cluster types are each attested in only one root, and two further clusters beginning labially and ending velarly fall outside Sherer's main cluster generalization.
normalized_environment: RARE CLUSTER EXCEPTIONS to dominant HOMORGANIC/APICAL_INITIAL pattern
exceptions_or_counterexamples: These are explicit exceptions/low-frequency types, not evidence that all place combinations are productive.

claim: Consonant sequences created across morpheme boundaries follow the same broad co-occurrence patterns as root-internal sequences.
normalized_environment: CLUSTER_COOCURRENCE generalized across ROOT_INTERNAL and MORPHEME_BOUNDARY domains
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Sherer's explicit rare lexical exceptions remain exceptions to the broad segmental generalization; this record does not imply identical token frequencies across domains.

time_scope: Eades 1979 stress description summarized by Sherer
claim: Stress falls on a long vowel if one is present; otherwise a syllable closed by a glide attracts stress. If neither condition applies, disyllables stress the first vowel and words of three or more syllables stress a non-final syllable. Non-glide codas do not attract stress.
formal_environment: stress by V-length > glide-coda > default nonfinal position
normalized_environment: STRESS_PRIORITY: LONG_VOWEL > GLIDE_CODA > DEFAULT; OTHER_CODA weight-insensitive
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Closing consonants other than glides explicitly fail to attract stress; Sherer notes that the moraic interpretation is analytical rather than forced by the descriptive facts.

claim: Eades reports only twenty monosyllabic roots; apart from the particle [waw] 'also' and a few verbs whose vowel length is unstable, the monosyllabic roots have long vowels.
normalized_environment: MONOSYLLABIC_ROOT strongly requires LONG_VOWEL, with particle and unstable-verb exceptions
exceptions_or_counterexamples: [waw] and a few verbs are explicitly exempt/unstable; therefore this is a strong lexical generalization, not an exceptionless surface ban.
section: 5.2.4 Minimal Words in Guugu Yimidhirr and Gumbaynggir

time_scope: Eades 1979 pp.348-354 lexical examples compiled by Sherer
claim: Long vowels are attested before medial consonant sequences ('hypercharacterized' syllables in Sherer's terminology), so vowel length is not categorically banned before clusters.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The examples establish permission, not unrestricted productivity for every long-vowel-plus-cluster combination.
publication_page: Sherer ch.5 p.8; examples from Eades 1979 pp.348-354
